findings.reason: the section's precondition must name every section whose fix its zeros depend on (through §17), or the census is run early and reports a defect it was meant to confirm is gone.
findings.text: §11 says it is "re-run once §2–§10 have landed and every producer has reloaded", but the figure it now adds — "zero `review-missing` duties sampled while their review run was live" — is the defect §16 repairs, and its lift/wait/landing figures are §12, §14, §15 and §17; followup `f-alwh-005` orders "§11 runs last". A node dispatched on §11's own stated precondition would measure an unfixed `review-missing` class and §12–§17's unfixed rows, then assert zeros against them.

findings.reason: without naming the resolver the census's zero is an artefact of the matcher rather than a finding, which is exactly the §16 case the section exists to measure.
findings.text: the sampler "reads the live review pointers at that moment" and copies one "when a live review stands for that run", but never names the reader that decides standing; §16 records the pointer behind the same defect carrying `reviewed_run_id: null` and `review_subject: null`, recognised only through `recovery_review_dispatch._review_subject` and its fallback `recovery_review_delivery._resolved_reviewed_run_id` (recovery_review_delivery.py:218). A sampler keyed on the raw `reviewed_run_id` field finds no standing review and reports zero by construction.

findings.reason: the node would either run a sampler past its own turn (which it cannot hold) or report a window it never sampled; the plan needs a slice/persistence rule for the sampler.
findings.text: the report requires sampling every session's obligations snapshot for "the 24 hours after the last producer reload", and the section itself states why this cannot be recovered later ("the per-session obligations snapshots are overwritten in place"); nothing in the section says where the samples are persisted or how a single node's run spans 24 hours of live sampling, so the finished report figure has no stated way to be produced inside a node's gate.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `ticker.stream_carries` (ticker.py:1363), `ticker._pane_word` (ticker.py:1346), `docs/evidence/...` paths and §1's "24 rows with `process_alive: true`" all resolve; no hrefs in this section.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the report needs a 24-hour *live* sampling window (snapshots are overwritten in place, per `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py`), and the section states no persisted sample store or way for one node's run to span that window.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — `scripts/census/` exists beside `death_census.py` and `carryover_census.py`, and both `docs/evidence/fragments/a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted/` and `docs/evidence/archive/a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted-landed.html` exist.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section names no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags for symbols; `<node-id>` is a runtime placeholder in an evidence path.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the sampler's criterion for "a live review stands for that run" is unnamed, while the plan's own §16 evidence records a pointer whose `reviewed_run_id`/`review_subject` were null.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11 names one deliverable, a committed census module with its test and report fragment.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §11's precondition still reads "re-run once §2–§10 have landed", but its new `review-missing` figure is fixed by §16 and its other figures by §12/§14/§15/§17, while followup `f-alwh-005` says "§11 runs last".
